Series::nextafter¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signature¶

Series::nextafter(const Series& other) const -> Series
Series& Series::nextafter_(const Series& other)

What It Does¶

nextafter() returns the next representable floating-point value after the receiver a, stepping toward other b.

The step is exactly one ULP (unit in the last place) — the smallest change the format can express at that magnitude. If a == b, the result is b unchanged.

This is a low-level tool. It is used to build a strict bound from a non-strict one (the smallest value strictly greater than x is nextafter(x, +inf)), to nudge a value off an exact boundary before a comparison, or to enumerate the representable grid near a point when testing numerical code.

Parameters¶

other (const Series&)

The direction to step. Only whether b is greater than, less than, or equal to a matters. Broadcasts against the receiver.

Returns¶

Series or Series& a advanced one representable step toward b. nextafter_() writes the result back into the receiver.

Gradient¶

nextafter() is not differentiable. It is a discrete step along the representable grid.

Examples¶

Example 1. Stepping up from 1.0 and down from 1.0. The change is one ULP, about 2.2e-16 at this magnitude, so a rounded printout still shows 1.

auto a = pluss::make_series({1.0, 1.0});
auto b = pluss::make_series({2.0, 0.0});

std::cout << a.nextafter(b);

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[2], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=2, contiguous=true)
data=[1, 1]

The two results differ from 1.0 and from each other in the last bit; the default formatting rounds both back to 1.

Example 2. Stepping from 0.0 toward a negative number lands on the smallest representable magnitude — a subnormal.

std::cout << pluss::make_series({0.0}).nextafter(pluss::make_series({-1.0}));

Output¶

pluss::Series(shape=[1], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=[-4.9406565e-324]

Example 3. Equal arguments leave the value unchanged.

pluss::series::print(
    std::cout,
    pluss::make_series({3.0}).nextafter(pluss::make_series({3.0})));

Output¶

Series(shape=[1], strides=[1], dtype=float64, platform=cpu, numel=1, contiguous=true)
data=[3.0000]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • The step size depends on magnitude. Near 1.0 it is about 2.2e-16; near 1e300 it is about 1e284. nextafter() is not “add a small constant.”

  • Only the direction of other is used, never its magnitude.

  • Not differentiable.

  • Floating-point inputs.

Summary¶

nextafter(a, b) is a moved one ULP toward b:

  • one representable step; a == b returns b

  • only the sign of b - a matters

  • not differentiable

See Also¶

  • Series::clamp_min / Series::clamp_max: for bounding by a value rather than nudging by one ULP.

  • Series::isfinite: checking the result stayed in range after a sequence of steps.
